methodology.location: isolated temporary databases; no application or production changes
methodology.foreground: one process: 150 real PrivateMessageStore sends and seen updates; another: 150 unread and history reads; 10ms pacing
methodology.sync: three concurrent processes, each 80 synthetic transactions: one 8 KiB placeholder bundle, 25 indexed items, one checkpoint; 10ms pacing
methodology.layouts: no-sync baseline; same database; separate database; both DELETE and WAL
limitations: Synthetic proposed storage shape, not implemented sync API or browser protocol
No source/target authorization or crypto cost measured
Small local sample with shared disk and process scheduling noise
Foreground samples include both overlapping and post-sync operations
60-second implicit local PDO busy timeout; zero errors is not a latency guarantee

counterexamples.scope: Abstract counterexample model, not implementation or crypto validation

planning_conclusions: Derive demand from current membership and account history; no durable request queue or approval ledger.
Retain encrypted transfers and indexes as authoritative private data.
Persist target-reported successful coverage to avoid redoing full history scans; it is a discardable scheduling hint, not proof of current readability.
Coverage must reference an available eligible grant or verified direct access; lost grants reopen gaps.
Retain a small resettable scan checkpoint per donor/account, including fair target/message traversal; restart-at-zero can starve later pages.
Permit bounded alternate candidates; an unverified upload never closes a gap.
Derive status counts; no durable counters, permanent failure claims, work leases, or general job queue.
Use dedicated tables in the configured private-message database unless representative concurrency verification fails.
Reuse approved-key resolver, identity/authentication, loader and original reader; chat envelope preparation automatically targets whole usernames and is unsuitable unchanged.
Gate donor enablement on measured foreground behavior, short transactions and an explicit supported journal/timeout policy.
